subject: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-15T17:12:00-04:00
Subject: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment: 

Summary of discovery
- Primary goal: replace rule-based intent routing in BrightCart's customer support flow with a lightweight intent classifier to surface the right fulfillment path (returns, payment issues, tech support).
- Volume: ~8k incoming messages/day, peak 120 req/min during promotions.
- Success metrics you called out: intent precision >= 89% (top intent), end-to-end routing latency < 220ms median, and <= 2% drop/fallback rate compared to baseline.

Proposed trial plan (3-week baseline)
1) Week 0 (kickoff): ingest 15k labeled samples (we'll provide a template), share trial config and ACLs.
2) Week 1-2 (validation): run model against historical and live shadow traffic; collect precision/recall and latency.
3) Week 3 (acceptance): evaluate against acceptance criteria, document regression tests.

Proposed acceptance criteria (initial)
- Intent precision (top-1): >= 89% on evaluation set (stratified by intent).
- Median inference latency (99th under baseline load): < 220ms.
- False-routing (customer hit fallback flow): <= 2% relative to current rule-based baseline.

Action items / ask from BrightCart
- Confirm you can share a 15k labeled sample export (CSV) by Tue 9/23. If you can only provide smaller samples, tell us which intents to prioritize.
- Confirm you’re OK with the shadow/live split we proposed (80/20).

Attachments: redwood_trial_plan_20250915.pdf and BrightCart_POC_acceptance_criteria_v2.xlsx (skeleton acceptance table)

If this looks good I’ll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Ben (CS) and we’ll update the plan with concrete owners & kickoff calendar invite.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Date: 2025-09-16T09:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case

Diego —

Thanks for the recap — this is very close to what we discussed. A couple items from our side after internal sync: 

1) Additional use case request: during the call our CS ops team pushed for "intent routing for payment disputes" to be included as a live route instead of shadow — it's a high-impact use case for reducing manual triage.
2) Data / privacy: we can share a 10k sample now but some rows will require PII redaction; can you confirm your redaction guidance?
3) Acceptance tweak: for routing that goes live (payment disputes), we need an extra guard — enable safe-fallback to manual triage for any low-confidence decisions and include an audit log of model decisions (timestamp, confidence, decision).

If we add the payment-dispute route to live in week 2, we'll need a 1-week extension on the overall trial to accommodate a controlled canary and post-canary analysis.

Happy to jump on 30m to walk through the audit/log schema with Marissa — Priya, will you be the internal owner for data delivery?

—Alex
Director, Product Ops | BrightCart

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-16T11:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case

Alex — great note, and totally reasonable asks. Looping in Marissa (solutions engineering) and Ben (CS) to scope the technical plan and logging requirements.

Proposed adjustments based on your ask:
- Add payment-dispute intent as a live canary in Week 2 (controlled 5% traffic initially).
- Add audit log requirement: we will produce a per-request audit record with request_id, top-3 intents, confidences, timestamp, and routing decision. For any low-confidence (< 0.45) we'll route to manual triage automatically.
- Extend trial by 1 week (total 4 weeks) to include canary + post-canary analysis.

Suggested owners:
- Data delivery: Priya Shah (BrightCart) — deliver CSV as discussed.
- Solution implementation & canary: Marissa Cole (Redwood).
- CSM / success metrics: Ben Carter (Redwood).
- AE / commercial: Diego Fernandez (Redwood).

I'll attach an updated acceptance spreadsheet with an additional sheet for the payment-dispute canary and a draft audit schema. Marissa — can you confirm the minimal fields you need for the CSV (we suggested: message_id, created_at, raw_text, label_intent, customer_id_hash)?

Next steps: once Priya confirms delivery date I’ll send a revised kickoff invite that includes the trial runbooks and the Meet link.

Thanks —
Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case

Hi all —

Quick technical note from the solutions side after reviewing the proposed change: happy to run payment-dispute as a live canary but we need the following minimal data columns for stable evaluation and traceability:
- message_id (string)
- created_at (ISO8601)
- raw_text (UTF-8 text) — PII redacted per your guidance
- label_intent (string) — historical ground truth where available
- customer_id_hash (string) — hashed, not reversible

Evaluation plan for payment-dispute live canary
- Canary cadence: start at 5% live traffic for 72 hours, escalate to 20% for next 72 hours if top-1 precision >= 92% and median latency < 200ms.
- Metrics to capture: top-1 precision, top-3 coverage, median latency, fallback rate, manual override rate.
- Logging: we will send an audit CSV export each day and a compressed debug bundle at the end of the canary window.

Operational asks
- Priya: please confirm redacted sample by 9/23 and indicate whether customer_id can be hashed at your end or if we should hash on ingest.
- Alex: confirm you’re comfortable with the two-step ramp (5% -> 20%) or propose a different ramp plan.

Suggested files attached: intent-routing-data-spec.csv (schema), updated acceptance criteria workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightcart.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan & acceptance criteria — intent routing use case

Marissa / Diego —

Thanks for the detail. We can provide a 10k redacted sample by 9/23; customer_id will be hashed on our side and we’ll strip any direct PII.

We agree to the canary ramp (5% -> 20%) with one caveat: BrightCart requires that any live routing for payment disputes meet a 95% confidence threshold before we escalate beyond 5% (we will accept Redwood’s low-confidence auto-fallback rule, but want the 95% guard for promotion).

Also request: please include a simple cost estimate line in the trial plan for the canary week (approx tokens/month and expected infra billing) so our procurement team has a quick number to review.

I’ll be the owner for data delivery and will send the sample via the secure SFTP link Diego mentioned on or before 9/23.

—Priya
Sr. Manager, Customer Ops | BrightCart

Subject: Final: Updated trial timeline, owners & kickoff

Alex / Priya —

Thanks everyone — updating the plan per thread:
- Trial length: 4 weeks (kickoff 9/24, acceptance by 10/22).
- Payment-dispute live canary: start 10/06 at 5% for 72 hours, promote to 20% only if top-1 precision >= 95% and median latency < 200ms.
- Audit logs: Redwood will supply daily audit CSVs and a compressed debug bundle after canary. Fields per intent-routing-data-spec.csv.
- Cost estimate: we attached a 1-page cost summary (approx $5k for the canary week based on expected volume) to redwood_trial_plan_20250915.pdf. Procurement note: Ben will be the point for any quick PO questions.

Owners recap:
- Data delivery: Priya Shah (BrightCart) — sample by 9/23 via SFTP.
- Solution & canary: Marissa Cole (Redwood).
- CSM / success: Ben Carter (Redwood).
- AE / commercial: Diego Fernandez (Redwood).

Kickoff: I’ve scheduled a 45m kickoff on 2025-09-24 11:00 AM ET — Meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abcq-123. Invite sent separately.

Next steps (this week)
- Priya: drop the sample on SFTP by 9/23.
- Marissa: confirm ingest schema and share the trial runbook by 9/19.
- Ben: confirm CSM monitoring dashboard and weekly checkpoint cadence.

If that all looks good I’ll mark the deal stage to "POC: kickoff scheduled" in HubSpot and share the updated acceptance criteria workbook.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to get started.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
